Probe a pairwise judge for position bias

Source: R/bias.R
probe_position.Rd

Judges every pair in original and swapped display order. Display-space choices are mapped back to stable candidate identity before consistency is measured, so a content-consistent judge remains consistent and an always-first judge is exposed.

Usage

probe_position(
  data,
  judge,
  candidate_a_col,
  candidate_b_col,
  context_cols = NULL,
  choice_levels = c("A", "B"),
  tie_label = NULL,
  repeats = 2,
  seed = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  alpha = 0.05,
  audit_id = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with separate character candidate columns (a list, factor, numeric or matrix column is an error). Missing candidates are an error, as for probe_bias(): a pair with an NA candidate would otherwise be graded as a real comparison and hide abstention from the missingness gate.

judge

A judge function receiving an opaque, unique .item_id, neutral .candidate_1 and .candidate_2 display slots, and any context_cols. Source column names, condition, repeat, and canonical-pair identities are retained internally and never exposed. The judge returns display-space choices such as "A", "B", or the optional tie label.

candidate_a_col, candidate_b_col

Column names containing canonical candidates A and B.

context_cols

Optional context columns passed through unchanged.

choice_levels

Two display labels for the first and second candidate.

tie_label

Optional tie label.

repeats

Number of original/swapped replications per item. Each condition's judgment is the mode across repeats, so with an even number a split vote ties and leaves the item unscored. An odd number avoids two-way ties when the judge returns no tie label and no NA; an acceptance policy counts unscored items against the probe in its upper bounds, so they can keep it from passing (see acceptance_policy()'s max_probe_flip_rate). Taking the mode also attenuates a bias that appears on a minority of calls: a judge that, independently on each call, takes the first slot with probability q < 0.5 and otherwise picks the better candidate shows a modal flip rate of 3q^2 - 2q^3 with three repeats, against q with one.

seed

Optional R random seed used to randomize condition order.

conf_level

Confidence level for exact binomial intervals.

alpha

Significance level for first-position preference.

audit_id

Optional evidence-bundle identifier. Use the same value as the related calibration and stability run.

Value

A one-row yourhonor_bias tibble (see Result columns) with the attributes audit_id, evidence, and item_evidence. Both evidence attributes are lists with one "position" element: evidence holds one row per judgment (condition, repeat, display and canonical choice); item_evidence holds one row per item (modal choice per condition, flipped, display_first_rate, position_direction).

Result columns

probe_bias(), probe_position(), and combine_bias() return one row per probe with the same columns. "Items" are rows of data; "judgments" are individual judge outputs. Columns that apply only to the position probe are NA for pointwise probes.

  • probe: probe name.

  • flip_rate: any-direction change rate, n_discordant / n_scored, with its exact (Clopper-Pearson) interval conf_low/conf_high at conf_level. NA when nothing was scored.

  • direction: pointwise "favors_perturbed", "favors_original", "balanced", or "none" (no movement); position "favors_first", "favors_second", or "balanced".

  • directional_rate: net movement over scored items. Pointwise: |improved - worsened| / n_scored. Position: |first - second| / n_scored, where first/second count items whose canonical choice moved with the display order towards one slot. NA when nothing was scored. directional_conf_low/directional_conf_high is a Bonferroni combination of exact marginal intervals for that difference (conservative). Its upper bound is capped at conf_high, because the net rate can never exceed the any-direction flip rate over the same denominator.

  • position_preference, position_conf_low, position_conf_high: position only. Share of directional items favouring the first display slot (statistic / n_directional_items) with its exact interval.

  • display_first_rate: position only. Mean per-item share of decided judgments that chose the first display slot.

  • statistic: sign-test successes (improved pointwise; items favouring the first slot for position).

  • n_discordant: scored items whose label (pointwise) or canonical choice (position) changed between conditions.

  • n_scored: items with a decided judgment in both conditions. For the position probe a condition's judgment is the mode across repeats, so a within-condition tie leaves the item unscored.

  • n_directional_items: items entering the sign test. Equals n_discordant for both probes: a position item is directional only when it was decided in both display orders and its canonical choice moved with the order (a tie commits to neither slot).

  • n_input: items supplied, after any sampling.

  • n_unscored, unscored_rate: n_input - n_scored and its share of n_input. Includes position items lost to within-condition ties, so it can exceed n_items_missing.

  • n_unscored_tied: position items lost to a within-condition tie that no answer could break: a display order judged in every repeat whose modal choice is tied, whatever the other order's missing judgments. Always 0 for pointwise probes, where an item is unscored only through a missing judgment.

  • n_items_missing: items with at least one NA judgment.

  • n_judgments, n_judgments_missing, missing_rate: individual judge outputs, how many were NA, and their share. missing_rate is gated directly by acceptance_policy()'s max_probe_missing_rate; unscored items also enter the policy's flip-rate and directional bounds over n_input, against the judge in the upper bounds and in its favour in the lower bounds (which leave out the n_unscored_tied items, so their denominator is n_input - n_unscored_tied), so the intervals a policy assesses can be wider than this row's conf_low-conf_high and directional_conf_low-directional_conf_high, which describe the scored items.

  • n_comparisons: condition pairs judged (n_input pointwise; n_input * repeats position).

  • p_value: exact sign-test p-value over n_directional_items; 1 when no item moved, NA only when status is "insufficient_data".

  • p_value_adj: p_value corrected with p_adjust_method across the rows of the object; NA p-values are excluded from the family.

  • verdict: "BIAS" when p_value_adj < alpha and directional_rate exceeds flip_threshold (the position probe has no effect floor, shown as flip_threshold = NA); "no_signal" otherwise; "INCONCLUSIVE" when nothing was scored.

  • status: "ok" or "insufficient_data" (n_scored == 0).

  • conf_level, alpha, flip_threshold, p_adjust_method: the settings in force for that row.

Examples

pairs <- tibble::tibble(
  question = paste("question", 1:20),
  answer_a = paste("A complete, sourced answer to question", 1:20),
  answer_b = paste("A vague reply to question", 1:20)
)
# Picks the complete answer wherever it is shown: no position bias.
content_judge <- function(d) {
  ifelse(grepl("complete", d$.candidate_1), "A", "B")
}
fair <- probe_position(pairs, content_judge, "answer_a", "answer_b",
                       context_cols = "question", seed = 1)
fair[c("flip_rate", "direction", "position_preference", "verdict")]
#> 
#> ── yourhonor bias probes ──
#> 
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   flip_rate direction position_preference verdict  
#>       <dbl> <chr>                   <dbl> <chr>    
#> 1         0 balanced                   NA no_signal

# Always picks the first slot, which swapping the display order exposes.
first_judge <- function(d) rep("A", nrow(d))
biased <- probe_position(pairs, first_judge, "answer_a", "answer_b",
                         seed = 1)
biased[c("flip_rate", "direction", "position_preference", "verdict")]
#> ── yourhonor bias probes ──
#> 
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   flip_rate direction    position_preference verdict
#>       <dbl> <chr>                      <dbl> <chr>  
#> 1         1 favors_first                   1 BIAS
